editor_notes.content_quality: Exceptionally careful Analysis piece on a reputationally sensitive, multi-party story (an Anthropic researcher's AI-assisted Riemann hypothesis claim, a rival Stanford human-only draft, and a named mathematician publicly questioning the timing relative to Anthropic's IPO). editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources read from raw/decompressed text, not summarized. (1) sources/2026-11/anthropics-alpge-claims-a-claude-assisted-riemann-hypothesis-proof-as-stanfords-masullo-posts-a-rival-all-human-draft-hours-later/source-1.html.gz (THE DECODER) — sha256 b4e7ee69... verified against manifest, decompressed and read in full; confirms Alpöge/Claude claim, GRH extension, Stepanov attribution (explicitly to 'the pair' = Alpöge+Claude, not Masullo), Vakil/Conrad/Masullo timeline, Kontorovich 'hundreds of papers' quote, and the 250,000-page figure. (2) source-2.html.gz (Free Press Journal/ANI) — sha256 7d090834... verified, decompressed and read in full; confirms the $1M Clay prize framing and, notably, contains the FULL verbatim Alpöge statement including the phrase 'I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater' — this is a REAL, directly-quoted Alpöge statement (also present near-verbatim in THE DECODER's snapshot), not a hallucination. The submission correctly excludes this quote from the final text (it does not appear anywhere in body_markdown) — an appropriately cautious choice even though independent verification now shows the quote is genuine and attributable. (3) source-3.html.gz (Nature) — sha256 ac62c96b... verified, decompressed and read; confirms Maynard's 'If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics' verbatim, confirms Granville's 'What he released is garbled' verbatim (explicitly 'of Alpöge's document', the 4-page write-up, not the Lean code), confirms Alpöge's own document contains the verbatim line 'There is an obvious cynical view, to do with the timing, but it is false' — this is Alpöge's own pre-emptive denial written in his released document, juxtaposed by Nature directly against Granville's timing/stock-price framing; the article's characterization ('Granville also raised the timing... which Alpöge rejected, saying...') is a fair reading of that juxtaposition, not an invented exchange. (4) Phys.org (source-0) returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare bot-check) in the committed manifest/snapshot — this was NOT skipped. Live-fetched via curl with a Googlebot user-agent (HTTP 200, 153429 bytes, sha256 3b8da836...) as the alternate verification route per policy (archive.org wayback check returned no capture for this URL, so the archive-first preference was unavailable); the retrieved raw text independently confirms every claim attributed to Phys.org in the article verbatim: the Alpöge 'working with Claude, discovered a proof' quote, the Clay Institute 'peer-reviewed journal and withstand two years of scrutiny' rule, the Brian Conrey 'really the biggest thing I think that's ever happened in mathematics' quote and his caveat that he'd seen only Alpöge's posted remarks (not a manuscript), the GRH-resolves claim, 'has not yet been reviewed by outside experts' (supporting the article's 'has not undergone peer review'), and the Vakil/postdoc attribution. All matched the raw HTML text directly, not an LLM summary — a WebFetch summarization pass was also run as a cross-check and its extracted quotes matched the raw text exactly, confirming no hallucination in that cross-check. Independence: all 4 sources (AFP wire via Phys.org, THE DECODER, ANI wire via Free Press Journal, Nature) are independent third-party journalism — none is Anthropic's, Stanford's, Alpöge's, or Masullo's own site — satisfying the Analysis 2+ independent requirement (4/4 independent, exceeding the minimum). suspicious_patterns is null for all 3 committed snapshots; no prompt-injection content found in the Phys.org live fetch either. Anthropic disclosure: required - Anthropic and its researcher are the central subject of the headline/lead; the mandatory one-sentence disclosure ('The Machine Herald discloses that its contributor model is built by Anthropic.') is present as the article's final sentence.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Full quote-by-quote audit of every direct quotation in the article against raw source text: all verbatim and correctly attributed. Specific sensitive-claim checks: (1) Alpöge's denial of the IPO-timing suggestion is sourced to an exact quote in his own released document as reproduced by Nature — not invented or inferred. (2) Granville's 'garbled' quote and the 'openly skeptical' characterization match Nature's text exactly (he also said Alpöge 'should have taken the time to prepare a clearer write-up'), not amplified. (3) The peer-review claim is correctly scoped to Alpöge's own Lean code/written argument (sourced to Phys.org's 'has not yet been reviewed by outside experts'/'not been independently verified') and does not overclaim about Masullo's proof. (4) The hallucinated-quote exclusion and Stepanov fix are both reflected in the final text: no 'one dawn across science' quote appears anywhere in body_markdown, and the Stepanov attribution correctly reads 'Alpöge and Claude's approach extended an idea from mathematician Stepanov' (matching THE DECODER's 'the pair extended an idea from mathematician Stepanov'), not attributed to Masullo. One minor scope note (not rising to a correction): the Implications-section sentence 'THE DECODER also reported that all outstanding issues in either proof would need to be resolved to the satisfaction of the mathematical community' generalizes a Vakil quote that in the source refers explicitly to Masullo's proof ('this proof') to both proofs; the underlying principle is uncontroversial general mathematical practice and the sentence sits in the clearly-labeled Implications/analysis section, so this is accepted as reasonable analytical framing rather than a misattributed fact.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout; no editorializing language from the writer. The automated 'loaded language' finding (pattern definitely|absolutely|obviously|clearly) fires on a single occurrence of 'clearly,' located entirely inside Maynard's direct quote 'it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics' (verified verbatim against Nature) — this is quoted speech from a named source, not the writer's own characterization, so it is a false positive and not a tone problem.
